# 佛說盂蘭盆經疏

**ID:** T1792
**Volume:** T39
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經疏部
**Byline:** 唐 宗密述
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 780–841
**Juans:** 2
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1792

## Contributors
- 宗密 (A000587)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T1792 in two fascicles is the most influential Tang Chinese commentary on *[the Yúlánpén jīng 盂蘭盆經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0364)* (T685), composed by the Huáyán-Chán synthesizer Guīfēng Zōngmì 圭峰宗密 (780–841), the Fifth Patriarch of the Huáyán school and one of the most important Tang Buddhist intellectuals. The opening preface — "始於混沌。塞乎天地。通人神。貫貴賤。儒釋皆宗之。其唯孝道矣" ("Beginning from primal chaos, filling Heaven and Earth, communicating the human and the spiritual, traversing the noble and the humble — what both Confucians and Buddhists ultimately venerate is filiality") — is one of the most famous statements of the Tang Buddhist case for the integration of Buddhist soteriology with the Confucian filial-piety tradition.

**Abstract**

[宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86)'s personal frame for the commentary is intensely autobiographical: "宗密罪釁早年喪親。每履雪霜之悲。永懷風樹之恨" ("I, Zōngmì, sinful as I am, lost my parents in my early years; whenever I tread on snow or frost I am pierced by sorrow, and forever I cherish the regret of the wind in the trees"). The reference to the *fēngshù* 風樹 of the *Hán shī wàizhuàn* — the lament of trees that wish to remain still while the wind blows on — is a classical Confucian topos for the grief of a son whose parents have died before he could fulfill his filial obligations. [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) thus presents the *Yúlánpén jīng* commentary as both Buddhist exegesis and personal *xiào* (filial-piety) practice. The commentary itself works through the parent text section by section, glossing terminological cruxes, locating the sūtra within the [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86)'s own *huìtōng* 會通 framework integrating Buddhism with Confucian ethics, and rooting the *Yúlán* offering in a continuous Buddhist account of *fútián* 福田 (fields of merit) inherited from the Mahāyāna.

Composition window: [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86)'s most productive period at Cǎotángsì 草堂寺 in the Zhōngnán Mountains and at the Tang capital, c. 820–841. No internal date is preserved, but the commentary cites his already-completed major works and is mentioned in [裴休](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A3%B4%E4%BC%91) Pèi Xiū's *Quánzhōng* 圭峰碑銘 (the inscription written shortly after [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86)'s death) as one of his canonical compositions. The work was the source-text for the cluster of Sòng sub-commentaries: [KR6i0367](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0367) (*Xīnjì* 新記 by [元照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E7%85%A7)), [KR6i0368](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0368) (*Huìgǔ tōngjīn jì* 會古通今記 by [普觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E8%A7%80)), [KR6i0369](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0369) (*Kē* 科 by [遇榮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%87%E6%A6%AE)) and the closely-related [KR6i0370](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0370) (*Xiàohéng chāo* 孝衡鈔 by [遇榮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%87%E6%A6%AE)), plus [KR6i0371](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0371) (*Yúyì* 餘義 by [日新](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%97%A5%E6%96%B0)) — together comprising one of the densest sub-commentary clusters in the entire Sòng Buddhist exegetical corpus.

Parent sūtra: [KR6i0364](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0364) (T685). Sòng sub-commentaries on this commentary: [KR6i0367](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0367) (X372), [KR6i0368](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0368) (X373), [KR6i0369](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0369) (X374), [KR6i0370](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0370) (X375), [KR6i0371](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0371) (X376).
